# Which radios a change builds and tests (tools/ci_scope.py reads this; README "CI" says how).
# A pull request runs a radio's workflow jobs when it changes a path in that radio's section;
# the other radios' jobs show as skipped. A push to main, the weekly run, "Run workflow" and a PR
# labelled ci-full build everything.
#
# One path a line, from the top of the repository. A line ending / (or a plain name, like sotto)
# takes everything inside it. * and ? stay inside one folder and ** crosses folders; a line with
# a wildcard matches files only (c/* is the files in c/, not c/k6/). A line starting ! takes a
# path back out (the last line that matches wins, as in .gitignore).
#
#   [ignore]   never builds anything (docs), unless a ! line takes the path back
#   [all]      builds every radio (the codec submodule, this map and its tool)
#   [<radio>]  that radio's sources, the tests its workflow runs and what they import, and its
#              own workflow file (one .github/workflows/ line a section)
# A path no section names builds every radio, and the Forbidden files job fails until it's added.
# That job (tools/ci_scope.py --check) also checks the Python each radio's tests import and the C
# its sources #include are in its section, and that no line has gone stale after a rename.
